question:
The document management system of a university needs to manage multiple types of documents. Each document type has a unique identifier and name, as well as a version number.
Each document type can have multiple status categories, such as "Lifecycle Status", "Approval Status", etc. Each status category has a corresponding version number and multiple statuses. Each status has a sequence number indicating its position in the process.
ddl:
-- Schema for database: rschema_0297

CREATE TABLE `document_types` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `version` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `status_categories` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `document_type_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `version` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`document_type_id`) REFERENCES `document_types` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `statuses` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `status_category_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `sequence` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`status_category_id`) REFERENCES `status_categories` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
